<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917980_theRebbe_758" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917980_theRebbe_758__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header for the maamar delivered on the last day of Pesach 5725.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">The last day of Pesach,</t>
    <t s="2">the year 5725.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verses describing Mashiach's coming, his personal quality, his leadership, and the resulting universal revelation of G-dliness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him... and he shall scent the fear of Hashem... and the wolf shall dwell with the lamb..."</t>
    <t s="1">And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, explains in his maamar beginning with the words "This"</t>
    <t s="2">that in these verses the prophet describes the coming of Mashiach our righteousness, who will come to redeem us speedily in our days,</t>
    <t s="3">and he states several things regarding King Mashiach and his conduct.</t>
    <t s="4">First, he explains the virtue of King Mashiach himself—"And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him,"</t>
    <t s="5">and afterwards he explains his conduct—"and he shall scent the fear of Hashem"</t>
    <t s="6">[for even "and he shall scent" is a matter of his conduct,</t>
    <t s="7">as in "he smells"</t>
    <t s="8">"and judges"],</t>
    <t s="9">and afterwards he adds "and the wolf shall dwell with the lamb,"</t>
    <t s="10">that the conduct of Mashiach will be in a manner that he will bring about</t>
    <t s="11">a revelation of G-dliness throughout the entire world,</t>
    <t s="12">not only in the speaking species but also in the living species</t>
    <t s="13">(wolf and leopard, etc.)</t>
    <t s="14">and even in the inanimate species,</t>
    <t s="15">and as the verse continues,</t>
    <t s="16">"For the earth shall be filled with knowledge of Hashem,"</t>
    <t s="17">that even the physical earth</t>
    <t s="18">(inanimate)</t>
    <t s="19">will be filled with knowledge of Hashem.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the distinction between the influence of a teacher and a king, their roots in Torah, and how Mashiach embodies both roles, revealing even transcendent matters as an encompassing light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the maamar points out,</t>
    <t s="1">that one must understand,</t>
    <t s="2">since the earth will then be filled with knowledge of Hashem,</t>
    <t s="3">why will a king be needed?</t>
    <t s="4">And the point of the explanation is</t>
    <t s="5">that kingship is a matter of exaltation,</t>
    <t s="6">that the king is separate and elevated from the people.</t>
    <t s="7">And even the commands of the king</t>
    <t s="8">(although ostensibly they are a movement of closeness,</t>
    <t s="9">that the king draws near to the people to lead them according to his will)</t>
    <t s="10">are</t>
    <t s="11">in a manner of elevation and separation,</t>
    <t s="12">in the way of a decree and command.</t>
    <t s="13">And so it is also from the side of the people,</t>
    <t s="14">that their fulfillment of the king's command is not because they know and comprehend the reason for the command,</t>
    <t s="15">but rather,</t>
    <t s="16">because of the fear and awe of the king,</t>
    <t s="17">that his awe be upon you.</t>
    <t s="18">Thus,</t>
    <t s="19">even the influence from the king to the people is in a manner of exaltation and separation.</t>
    <t s="20">And this is the difference between the influence of a teacher and the influence of a king,</t>
    <t s="21">that the matter of a teacher's influence is that the teacher draws close to the student</t>
    <t s="22">(contracting his intellect according to the vessel of the student)</t>
    <t s="23">in a way that the student will comprehend the intellect,</t>
    <t s="24">but not so the influence of a king, which is separate from the people,</t>
    <t s="25">above their intellect.</t>
    <t s="26">And the root of these two matters</t>
    <t s="27">(the influence of a teacher and of a king)</t>
    <t s="28">is</t>
    <t s="29">also in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="30">for there are in it</t>
    <t s="31">(analogous to)</t>
    <t s="32">these two matters.</t>
    <t s="33">For there are matters in the Torah that are clothed in intellect,</t>
    <t s="34">but the essence of the Torah is above intellect.</t>
    <t s="35">And in the future to come,</t>
    <t s="36">both matters will be revealed.</t>
    <t s="37">For this is why Mashiach is called by the name "teacher" and by the name "king,"</t>
    <t s="38">meaning,</t>
    <t s="39">that in addition to Mashiach teaching Torah to all of Israel</t>
    <t s="40">and influencing upon them good taste and knowledge in the secrets,</t>
    <t s="41">in the inner dimension of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="42">due to which influence Mashiach is called by the name "teacher,"</t>
    <t s="43">he himself will attain infinitely more than what he will influence in comprehension,</t>
    <t s="44">and the influence of these matters will be in the aspect of makif (encompassing light),</t>
    <t s="45">analogous to the influence of a king.</t>
    <t s="46">And one may add, seemingly,</t>
    <t s="47">that based on what is known</t>
    <t s="48">that the Torah study of Mashiach</t>
    <t s="49">(what he will teach all the people)</t>
    <t s="50">will be in a manner of vision that is above comprehension,</t>
    <t s="51">it is understood from this,</t>
    <t s="52">that the matters he will influence in the manner of a king are matters that cannot come into revelation even in a vision above intellect,</t>
    <t s="53">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="54">because Mashiach will be</t>
    <t s="55">(also)</t>
    <t s="56">a king,</t>
    <t s="57">he will reveal to Israel even these matters,</t>
    <t s="58">except that the revelation of these matters will be in the way of makif (encompassing light).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
